# Sanitizer Matrix & Disk Constraints Checklist: Comprehensive live QuickFIX interop conversation

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the four-configuration matrix, the TSan bring-up clause, the targeted-build requirement, and the disk-preflight contract (FR-021…FR-023b, D-1…D-11).
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) §Disk preflight · [contracts/disk-preflight.md](../contracts/disk-preflight.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

> ⚠️ The disk gate is itself an instance of the instrument-integrity class: the reading a builder would
> naturally take (`df` inside WSL) is blind to the constraint that actually binds. These items test
> whether the requirements make that non-obvious enough to survive an implementer's common sense.

## Configuration Vocabulary

- [ ] CHK001 Is the four-config set (`normal`, `asan`, `ubsan`, `tsan`) stated once normatively, with every artifact carrying the old three-value vocabulary enumerated for correction? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021a]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the mapping from configuration name to build preset specified as a value, so that a preset which does not enable what its name claims is a defect rather than a judgment call? [Measurability, Plan §External obligations]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for the **pre-existing** `asan-ubsan` rows already committed — specifically that re-characterising them is **out of scope** and belongs in a filed issue? [Clarity, Plan §External obligations]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the requirement that each of the four configs emit its **own** result row stated with folding named as a violation? [Completeness, Contract §E-4]

## TSan Bring-Up

- [ ] CHK005 Is TSan specified as **bring-up, not a config flip**, with the distinction made concrete rather than asserted? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements defined for the case where the TSan arm does not come up at all — specifically that this is a **finding to record and resolve**, not grounds to mark the arm `n/a`? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the mechanism by which instrumentation could break a passing session (timing changes moving heartbeat and test-request cadence) stated, so a failure is diagnosable rather than mysterious? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the requirements clear that only fixpp is sanitizer-instrumented and the counterparties run as unmodified binaries? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the **second bound** required to be stated wherever a sanitizer result is reported, rather than once in the spec? [Coverage, Spec §FR-023b]
- [ ] CHK010 Are requirements defined for showing each sanitizer arm **genuinely ran** the conversation, as distinct from reporting clean? [Measurability, Spec §SC-011]

## Disk Preflight — Predicate Design

- [ ] CHK011 Are the two predicates specified as evaluated **independently**, with the failure mode of collapsing them into one stated? [Clarity, Contract §D-1]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the output required to **name the failing predicate**, rather than reporting a generic failure? [Measurability, Contract §D-1a]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the requirement that the gate **exit non-zero and refuse the build** stated together with its negatives — no warn-and-continue, no exit 0 on the failing path? [Clarity, Contract §D-5]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements defined for an unreadable or absent host mount on WSL as a **FAIL**, never `proceed`? [Edge Case, Contract §D-3]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the off-WSL case specified as a **different** case rather than as a degenerate one, so that skipping the host predicate there does not weaken the WSL rule? [Consistency, Contract §D-4]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the host mount required to be resolved **independently**, with fallback to the build mount named as a violation? [Completeness, Contract §D-10]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for an unset or unparseable threshold as a **hard error, never 0**? [Edge Case, Contract §D-9]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the exclusion of the ccache device from both readings stated with the reason (a different device whose free space is not the constraint)? [Clarity, Contract §D-11]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for the reserve ballast **not** being counted as available, and for refilling it if spent? [Coverage, Plan §Reserve ballast]

## Threshold Provenance

- [ ] CHK020 Are both required values required to come from **measurement**, per configuration, against the **targeted** build — not from an estimate or a round number? [Measurability, Contract §D-7]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the rule that `required_host_growth` may **not** be derived from or offset against the internal figure stated explicitly? [Clarity, Contract §D-7a]
- [ ] CHK022 Are the measurement values required to carry their **date**, given that they move? [Completeness, Contract §D-6]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the bootstrap problem — the measurement cannot run under its own gate — specified with a resolution, rather than left as a circularity? [Conflict, Contract §D-9a]
- [ ] CHK024 Do the requirements state the mechanism (a growing VHD that does not auto-shrink) clearly enough that the reclaim procedure is understood rather than cargo-culted? [Clarity, Plan §The mechanism]
- [ ] CHK025 Is it stated that deleting inside the guest frees blocks for **reuse** but does **not** return space to the host, so that "delete a build tree to give the host its space back" is excluded? [Ambiguity, Plan §The mechanism]

## Matrix Sequencing

- [ ] CHK026 Is the requirement that builds be **targeted** rather than `all` stated with its magnitude, so it reads as the primary lever rather than an optimisation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023a]
- [ ] CHK027 Are requirements defined for the sequencing constraint that all four configurations may **not** fit simultaneously, with the ordering that resolves it? [Completeness, Plan §Matrix sequencing]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the reclaim order specified, together with the configuration that is **never** deleted and why? [Clarity, Plan §Reclaim procedure]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for what happens when the preflight cannot be satisfied **even after reclaim** — stop and report, with no partial build recorded as a pass or a skip? [Edge Case, Plan §When the preflight cannot be satisfied]
- [ ] CHK030 Is a run that died on `ENOSPC` required to be distinguishable from a genuine result at every layer that records an outcome? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014a]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK031 Does any requirement in this domain quote a measured size, count or free-space figure without a date and a re-derivation recipe? [Clarity, Gap]
- [ ] CHK032 Are the gate's own RED arms specified as requirements, rather than as an appendix a reader may treat as optional? [Completeness, Contract §Required RED arms]
- [ ] CHK033 Do the disk requirements and the promotion-ordering requirements agree on when a configuration's build tree may be reclaimed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014b]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
